name: Ken Hensley
milestone_by_age_26: Released two albums with The Gods on Columbia/EMI (Genesis in 1968, To Samuel a Son in 1969) and held a residency at the Marquee club in London while supporting major acts like Cream.
early_history_summary: Hensley learned guitar at age 12 from a Bert Weedon manual and played his first gig at 15 in Stevenage. He formed several local bands before creating The Gods in early 1965 with Mick Taylor and Greg Lake, writing most of the material and playing Hammond B3 organ. The Gods were signed by EMI and recorded at Abbey Road, releasing two albums before Hensley moved on to Toe Fat and eventually joined Uriah Heep in 1970.
primary_leverage_engine: Early specialization in songwriting and keyboards
family_context_summary: Son of a naval officer who gave his children a strict Victorian religious upbringing; family moved from Plumstead to Stevenage in 1945. No evidence of musical family background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early gigging, London rock scene, peer network with future stars, British rock wave
evidence_summary: Hensley started playing guitar at 12 and was gigging regularly by 15 in Stevenage, building years of reps before forming The Gods at 19 with future stars Mick Taylor and Greg Lake. His proximity to the London rock scene and the broader British rock explosion of the 1960s provided structural momentum. The Gods secured a deal with EMI/Columbia, recorded at Abbey Road, and supported Cream, giving Hensley professional recording and performance experience by his early twenties. No evidence of family musical background or financial privilege; his advantage was largely self-created through early practice and strategic peer connections.
starting_point: Born to a naval officer's family in Plumstead, south-east London; strict Victorian religious upbringing; family relocated to Stevenage, Hertfordshire in 1945.
current_position: Died on 4 November 2020 in Agost, Spain at age 75; final role was active musician touring with Ken Hensley & Live Fire.

trajectory.event: Formed The Gods with Mick Taylor and Greg Lake, beginning his professional music career in London.
Released debut album Genesis with The Gods on Columbia/EMI, recorded at Abbey Road Studios.
Joined Uriah Heep as keyboardist and primary songwriter, helping transform their sound from blues to progressive rock.
Uriah Heep released Demons and Wizards; Hensley wrote the hit single Easy Livin', achieving international recognition.
Left Uriah Heep after a decade as the band's creative linchpin, embarking on a solo career.
Died on 4 November 2020 in Agost, Spain, after a career spanning 60 years in music.

milestone_by_age_26: Won Miss Universe 1987 on May 26, 1987 in Singapore, becoming the first Chilean to win the title.
early_history_summary: Bolocco was born in Santiago to an Arbëreshë businessman father and attended the private Santiago College before briefly studying civil engineering and then costume design at INCA-CEA Institute. She was selected Miss Chile on April 20, 1987, and six weeks later won Miss Universe 1987, beating 67 contestants.
family_context_summary: Born to Enzo Bolocco Cintolesi, an Arbëreshë businessman, and Rose Marie Fonck Assler in Santiago, Chile. Attended private Santiago College, suggesting middle-to-upper-class background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: private school education, business family background, pageant pipeline, physical beauty
evidence_summary: Bolocco came from a comfortable background in Santiago, attending the private Santiago College and briefly studying engineering before switching to costume design. Her father was a businessman, providing a middle-to-upper-class platform. Her Miss Universe win at 22 was largely driven by physical attributes and poise rather than years of specialized training. The Chilean pageant pipeline and her private school education provided modest institutional support, but there is no evidence of sustained coaching or deep domain preparation before the milestone.
starting_point: Born in Santiago, Chile to Enzo Bolocco Cintolesi, an Arbëreshë businessman, and Rose Marie Fonck Assler; attended private Santiago College, suggesting a comfortable middle-to-upper-class family.
current_position: Living in Chile; married José Patricio Daire Barrios in 2022; former TV host and actress, now largely out of the public spotlight.

name: Mamo Wolde
milestone_by_age_26: Competed at the 1956 Melbourne Olympics at age 24 in 800m, 1500m, and 4x400m relay but did not win medals or distinguish himself; his major achievements (Olympic marathon gold, 10K silver) came at age 36 in 1968.
early_history_summary: Wolde was born in rural Ethiopia and moved to Addis Ababa in 1951. He joined the Imperial Guard and served as a peacekeeper in Korea from 1953-1955. He competed at the 1956 Olympics as a middle-distance runner but without notable results. His transition to long-distance running and international success began in the early 1960s, with his Olympic marathon gold coming in 1968 at age 36.
family_context_summary: Born in Ada'a to an Oromo family in rural Ethiopia; younger brother Demissie Wolde also became an international distance runner. Joined the Imperial Guard after moving to Addis Ababa.
evidence_summary: Wolde's Olympic debut at the 1956 Melbourne Games at age 24 yielded no medals and no notable performances (7th in 800m heat, 11th in 1500m heat). His material success — Olympic marathon gold and 10K silver — came at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics when he was 36. While Olympic participation is verifiable, it does not constitute a material success milestone by age 26.

name: Lasse Kjus
milestone_by_age_26: Won gold in the combined event at the 1993 FIS World Championships in Morioka, Japan, marking his senior-level international breakthrough.
early_history_summary: Kjus took up skiing at age seven in Norway, coached initially by Finn Aamodt, father of his friend and future skiing rival Kjetil André Aamodt. By 1990, at age 19, he won medals in all five events at the World Junior Championships and made his World Cup debut. His senior breakthrough came in 1993 with the World Championship gold in combined, followed by Olympic gold in combined at Lillehammer in 1994.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Oslo, Norway; took up skiing at age seven. His first coach was Finn Aamodt, father of his friend Kjetil André Aamodt, suggesting a family embedded in the Norwegian skiing community. No evidence of unusual family wealth.
parent_family_domain_summary: First coach was Finn Aamodt, father of friend and future skiing champion Kjetil André Aamodt, indicating proximity to Norwegian skiing expertise from childhood.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Norwegian ski culture, early coaching, national team pipeline, peer rivalry with Aamodt, all-discipline talent, overcame injuries
evidence_summary: Kjus grew up in Norway, one of the world's premier alpine skiing nations, and began skiing at age seven under the guidance of Finn Aamodt, father of his friend and future champion Kjetil André Aamodt. This gave him early access to elite coaching and a peer-level rival who pushed his development. By 19, he was winning medals across all five alpine disciplines at the World Junior Championships and had debuted on the World Cup circuit. The Norwegian national ski team pipeline provided a direct path to the elite level. He overcame a severe shoulder injury in 1991 and later a congenital nasal condition, demonstrating resilience. His all-discipline talent was rare and directly catalytic to his success.
starting_point: Born in Oslo, Norway; took up skiing at age seven, coached by Finn Aamodt, father of his friend and future champion Kjetil André Aamodt, indicating a family embedded in the Norwegian skiing community.
current_position: Retired from competitive skiing in 2006 at age 35; lives in Oslo, Norway; considered one of the most successful alpine skiers in history with 16 Olympic and World Championship medals.

trajectory.event: Won medals in all five events at the World Junior Championships and made his World Cup debut.
Won gold in the combined event at the FIS World Championships in Morioka, Japan, his senior international breakthrough.
Won Olympic gold in the combined event at the Lillehammer Winter Olympics, heading a Norwegian medal sweep.
Won his first overall World Cup title, cementing his status as the world's top alpine skier.
Won five medals at the World Championships in Vail (2 gold, 3 silver) and claimed his second overall World Cup title.
Retired from competitive skiing after the Torino Olympics, ending a 17-season career.

name: Peter Mansfield
milestone_by_age_26: Completed a First Class Honours degree in physics from Queen Mary College in 1959 at age 25-26, but his pioneering MRI work did not begin until the early 1970s; Nobel Prize came in 2003 at age 70.
early_history_summary: Mansfield was born in Lambeth, London, to a gas fitter father and left school at 15 to work as a printer's assistant. He developed an interest in rocketry, joined the Rocket Propulsion Department at 18, and studied A-levels at night school before entering Queen Mary College to study physics in 1956. He graduated with First Class Honours in 1959 and completed his PhD in 1962, but his MRI research did not begin until the 1960s-70s.
family_context_summary: Born in Lambeth, London, to Sidney George Mansfield, a gas fitter, and Rose Lillian Mansfield. Youngest of three brothers; grew up in Camberwell and spent war years as an evacuee. Left school at 15 with no formal qualifications.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; father was a gas fitter, no evidence of scientific or academic family background.
evidence_summary: Mansfield's early life was marked by humble origins — son of a gas fitter, left school at 15, worked as a printer's assistant. He entered university at 23 and graduated with First Class Honours at 25-26, but this academic qualification is not a material public milestone of success. His pioneering NMR/MRI research began in the 1960s-70s, with the first MRI images in 1974 and the Nobel Prize in 2003. No material, independently verifiable milestone of scientific achievement occurred by age 26.

name: Kalpana Chawla
milestone_by_age_26: Completed PhD in aerospace engineering in 1988 at age 26 and began work at NASA Ames Research Center, but astronaut selection came in December 1994 at age 32 and first space flight in 1997 at age 35; no material public milestone by age 26.
early_history_summary: Chawla was born in Karnal, India, to a tire manufacturing plant owner. She earned a bachelor's in aeronautical engineering from Punjab Engineering College in 1982, a master's from University of Texas in 1984, and a PhD from University of Colorado in 1988. She then joined NASA Ames as a researcher. Her astronaut selection came in 1994 and her first spaceflight in 1997.
family_context_summary: Born in Karnal, India, to Banarsi Lal Chawla, owner of a tire manufacturing plant, and Sanjogta Kharbanda. Family were Punjabi Hindu refugees from West Punjab during Partition. Father initially discouraged her interest in aerospace engineering.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father owned a tire manufacturing plant, indicating a business family with some financial means, but no direct aerospace or scientific domain expertise in the family.
evidence_summary: Chawla completed her PhD at age 26 and began a research position at NASA Ames, but these are academic qualifications rather than material public milestones. Her defining achievements — NASA astronaut selection (1994), first spaceflight as the first Indian-origin woman in space (1997), and the Columbia disaster (2003) — all occurred well after age 26. While her educational path was impressive, no independently verifiable material milestone of public success occurred by age 26.

name: Vin Diesel
milestone_by_age_26: Made stage debut at age 7 and appeared as an uncredited extra in Awakenings (1990) at age 23, but his first significant film work (Multi-Facial) was made in 1994 at age 27 and screened at Cannes in 1995 at age 28; breakthrough with Saving Private Ryan came in 1998 at age 31.

He remained involved in theater through adolescence, worked as a bouncer, and attended Hunter College for creative writing. After struggling to find acting roles, he made his own short film Multi-Facial in 1994 (age 27), which launched his career when Spielberg noticed it.
family_context_summary: Born Mark Sinclair Vincent in Alameda County, California; raised by mother Delora (an astrologer) and stepfather Irving Vincent (a drama teacher and theater director) in New York City. Has a twin brother, Paul. Biological father left before birth. Stepfather's theater background provided early exposure to performing arts.
parent_family_domain_summary: Stepfather Irving Vincent was a drama teacher and theater director, providing direct domain exposure to acting and theater from a young age.
evidence_summary: Diesel had early theater exposure from age 7 thanks to his stepfather's involvement in theater, and he appeared in an uncredited film role in 1990 at age 23. However, his first material milestone — writing, directing, producing, and starring in Multi-Facial — occurred in 1994 at age 27, after the age 26 cutoff. name: Jānis Krūmiņš
milestone_by_age_26: Won the USSR Premier League championship with ASK Riga in 1955 at age 25, beginning a run of four consecutive national titles (1955-1958) as the first dominant giant center in European basketball.
early_history_summary: Krūmiņš was born in rural Latvia and lost his father as a boy. He worked as a tree resin collector from age 13, standing 2 meters tall by age 14. Despite no basketball background, he was discovered by coach Alexander Gomelsky in 1953 at age 23 and brought to ASK Riga. Gomelsky personally trained him for up to 2 hours before each team session, and within two years Krūmiņš was a national champion and the dominant center in Soviet basketball.
family_context_summary: Born in Raiskums Parish, Latvia; father was a big strong man who died when Jānis was still a boy. Worked as a tree resin collector from age 13. Grew up in rural poverty with no connection to organized sports.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; father died when Jānis was young, no evidence of basketball or sports background in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: exceptional height (220cm), dedicated coaching by Gomelsky, Soviet sports pipeline, late start, rural poverty
evidence_summary: Krūmiņš's career was defined by two extraordinary factors: his exceptional height (220cm, rare for the era) and the dedicated mentorship of coach Alexander Gomelsky, who personally trained him for up to 2 hours before each team session and considered Krūmiņš his only true apprentice. Despite starting basketball at 23 with no prior experience, his physical dominance under the basket was immediate. He came from rural poverty — father died young, worked as a resin collector from 13 — and had no basketball background. The Soviet sports system provided the institutional pipeline, but his physical edge and Gomelsky's coaching were the decisive catalysts.
starting_point: Born in Raiskums Parish, rural Latvia; father died when he was a boy; worked as a tree resin collector from age 13; stood 2 meters tall by age 14 with no connection to organized sports.
current_position: Died on 20 November 1994 in Riga, Latvia at age 64; final role was retired basketball player who had played for ASK Riga (1954-1964) and VEF Riga (1964-1969).

trajectory.event: Discovered by coach Alexander Gomelsky and brought to ASK Riga, beginning his basketball career with no prior experience.

Won EuroBasket gold with the Soviet Union national team, the first of three consecutive European championships.
Won his third Olympic silver medal at the Tokyo Olympics, completing a remarkable international career.
Died on 20 November 1994 in Riga, Latvia.

name: Anita Ekberg
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Golden Globe for New Star of the Year (Actress) in 1956 at age 24 for her role in Blood Alley, and appeared in the Paramount production War and Peace the same year.
early_history_summary: Ekberg was born in Malmö, Sweden, the sixth of eight children. She worked as a fashion model in her teens and won Miss Sweden in 1950 at age 18, which led to a trip to the US for the 1951 Miss Universe pageant. As a finalist, she earned a starlet contract with Universal Studios, appeared in several films in 1953, and was signed by John Wayne's Batjac production company, leading to her Golden Globe win in 1956.
family_context_summary: Born in Malmö, Sweden, the sixth of eight children. No evidence of family wealth or entertainment industry connections. Mother encouraged her to enter the Miss Malmö competition in 1950.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family connections to entertainment or modeling.

The Hollywood studio system provided training in drama, elocution, and other skills, though she reportedly skipped many lessons. Her modeling experience in Sweden gave her some domain exposure. By 24, she had won a Golden Globe as New Star of the Year and appeared in War and Peace. Her family was large but not wealthy, and her success was primarily driven by her physical attributes rather than family advantage or deep skill development.
starting_point: Born in Malmö, Sweden, the sixth of eight children; no evidence of family wealth or entertainment connections; mother encouraged her to enter the Miss Malmö competition in 1950.

She worked as an international model across Europe and the US before returning to Venezuela and winning Miss Venezuela 2007, which led to her Miss Universe 2008 victory.
